title: Vertebrates: a Brake, a Clock and Identity

scenes.visual: Title card: Vertebrates: a Brake, a Clock and Identity.

scenes.tts: In the vertebrate neural tube, the cells are already neural. So what do the same parts do there?
scenes.visual: Neural tube cross-section with dividing progenitors. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: In the vertebrate neural tube, the cells are already neural. So what do the same parts do there?

scenes.tts: Here, proneural factors push a progenitor to become a neuron. Notch holds its neighbours back as progenitors.
scenes.visual: One progenitor leaves to become a neuron; its neighbours stay dividing.
scenes.narration: Here, proneural factors push a progenitor to become a neuron. Notch holds its neighbours back as progenitors.

scenes.tts: The vertebrate relatives of Enhancer of split are the Hess genes. Hess inhibits proneural genes.
scenes.caption: The vertebrate relatives of Enhancer of split are the Hes genes. Hes inhibits proneural genes.
scenes.visual: Family tree: E(spl) to Hes. A Hes repressor dims a proneural gene.
scenes.narration: The vertebrate relatives of Enhancer of split are the Hes genes. Hes inhibits proneural genes.

scenes.tts: Progenitors make Notch, its ligand Delta-like one, the repressors Hess one and Hess five, and proneural factors.
scenes.caption: Progenitors make Notch, its ligand Dll1, the repressors Hes1 and Hes5, and proneural factors.
scenes.visual: Labels on a progenitor: Notch, Dll1, Hes1, Hes5, Ascl1, Neurog2.
scenes.narration: Progenitors make Notch, its ligand Dll1, the repressors Hes1 and Hes5, and proneural factors.

scenes.tts: A cell that starts to differentiate raises Delta-like one. That keeps the progenitors around it as progenitors.
scenes.caption: A cell that starts to differentiate raises Dll1. That keeps the progenitors around it as progenitors.
scenes.visual: One cell raises Dll1; neighbours' Notch lights up and they stay as progenitors.
scenes.narration: A cell that starts to differentiate raises Dll1. That keeps the progenitors around it as progenitors.

scenes.tts: Neurons first appear spaced apart. New ones arise in the gaps, and cells leave the pool over days.
scenes.visual: Neurons appear spaced along the tube, then new ones fill the gaps over a day counter.
scenes.narration: Neurons first appear spaced apart. New ones arise in the gaps, and cells leave the pool over days.

scenes.tts: So lateral inhibition here is a brake on how fast progenitors are used up. A cell held back stays a dividing progenitor, and can compete again later.
scenes.visual: Label: a brake. A held-back progenitor divides and re-enters the contest.
scenes.narration: So lateral inhibition here is a brake on how fast progenitors are used up. A cell held back stays a dividing progenitor, and can compete again later.

scenes.tts: Is Notch in the stem cell or the non-stem cell? Both cells have the receptor.
scenes.visual: Two progenitors, both with Notch crescents.
scenes.narration: Is Notch in the stem cell or the non-stem cell? Both cells have the receptor.

scenes.tts: The cell whose Notch is more strongly activated stays a progenitor. The cell that keeps sending more Delta differentiates.
scenes.visual: The high-Notch cell stays a progenitor; the cell with steadily high Delta becomes a neuron.
scenes.narration: The cell whose Notch is more strongly activated stays a progenitor. The cell that keeps sending more Delta differentiates.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking Hess one make neurons too early, and have severe neural tube defects.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking Hes1 make neurons too early, and have severe neural tube defects.
scenes.visual: Hes1 knockout neural tube: neurons crowd in early; the tube is malformed.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking Hes1 make neurons too early, and have severe neural tube defects.

scenes.tts: Remove Hess five as well, and progenitors are lost still faster.
scenes.caption: Remove Hes5 as well, and progenitors are lost still faster.
scenes.visual: The progenitor pool shrinks faster.
scenes.narration: Remove Hes5 as well, and progenitors are lost still faster.

scenes.tts: Then a surprise about timing. In cultured cells, Hess one rises and falls about every two hours.
scenes.caption: Then a surprise about timing. In cultured cells, Hes1 rises and falls about every two hours.
scenes.visual: A trace of Hes1 oscillating. On screen: period about 2 hours, cultured cells.
scenes.narration: Then a surprise about timing. In cultured cells, Hes1 rises and falls about every two hours.

scenes.tts: Hess one represses its own gene. Its RNA and protein are short-lived, and making new protein takes time.
scenes.caption: Hes1 represses its own gene. Its RNA and protein are short-lived, and making new protein takes time.
scenes.visual: A loop diagram: gene, RNA, protein, back to gene with a minus sign. A delay clock on the arrow.
scenes.narration: Hes1 represses its own gene. Its RNA and protein are short-lived, and making new protein takes time.

scenes.tts: In mouse neural progenitors, Hess one oscillates too. Neurogenin two and Delta-like one cycle in the opposite phase.
scenes.caption: In mouse neural progenitors, Hes1 oscillates too. Neurog2 and Dll1 cycle in the opposite phase.
scenes.visual: Three traces: Hes1 up while Neurog2 and Dll1 are down, and the reverse. On screen: period about 2 to 3 hours.
scenes.narration: In mouse neural progenitors, Hes1 oscillates too. Neurog2 and Dll1 cycle in the opposite phase.

scenes.tts: In cells becoming neurons, Hess one falls, and Neurogenin two stays high. So a brief pulse of Delta is not a commitment.
scenes.caption: In cells becoming neurons, Hes1 falls, and Neurog2 stays high. So a brief pulse of Delta is not a commitment.
scenes.visual: One cell's Hes1 trace drops; its Neurog2 trace stays up.
scenes.narration: In cells becoming neurons, Hes1 falls, and Neurog2 stays high. So a brief pulse of Delta is not a commitment.

scenes.tts: Predict. In cultured progenitors, use light to hold A S C L one steady, or make it oscillate. Which become neurons?
scenes.caption: Predict. In cultured progenitors, use light to hold Ascl1 steady, or make it oscillate. Which become neurons?
scenes.visual: Prompt card: cultured mouse progenitors. Ascl1 steady versus Ascl1 oscillating. Two traces, two blank outcomes.
scenes.narration: Predict. In cultured progenitors, use light to hold Ascl1 steady, or make it oscillate. Which become neurons?

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: Steady A S C L one pushed cells to become neurons. Oscillating A S C L one kept them dividing as progenitors.
scenes.caption: Steady Ascl1 pushed cells to become neurons. Oscillating Ascl1 kept them dividing as progenitors.
scenes.visual: Reveal: the steady trace leads to neurons; the oscillating trace leads to dividing progenitors. Label: Imayoshi and colleagues, 2013, cultured mouse progenitors.
scenes.narration: Steady Ascl1 pushed cells to become neurons. Oscillating Ascl1 kept them dividing as progenitors.

scenes.tts: Last question. Does a proneural factor also decide what kind of neuron forms?
scenes.visual: Forebrain cross-section: Neurog2 dorsal, Ascl1 ventral.
scenes.narration: Last question. Does a proneural factor also decide what kind of neuron forms?

scenes.tts: In the mouse forebrain, Neurogenin two is high in dorsal progenitors. A S C L one is high in ventral ones.
scenes.caption: In the mouse forebrain, Neurog2 is high in dorsal progenitors. Ascl1 is high in ventral ones.
scenes.visual: Dorsal cortex shaded for Neurog2, ventral eminences shaded for Ascl1.
scenes.narration: In the mouse forebrain, Neurog2 is high in dorsal progenitors. Ascl1 is high in ventral ones.

scenes.tts: Researchers swapped them, each into the other's place. Predict. Does the factor carry the identity, or the territory?
scenes.visual: Prompt card: swap the coding regions. Two rows: if the factor carries identity; if the territory does.
scenes.narration: Researchers swapped them, each into the other's place. Predict. Does the factor carry the identity, or the territory?

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: Neither, fully. A S C L one pushed dorsal cells partly ventral.
scenes.caption: Neither, fully. Ascl1 pushed dorsal cells partly ventral.
scenes.visual: Reveal: dorsal cells with Ascl1 switch on some ventral markers.
scenes.narration: Neither, fully. Ascl1 pushed dorsal cells partly ventral.

scenes.tts: In the ventral forebrain, Neurogenin two restored neurons, but did not push them dorsal. The swaps were not mirror images.
scenes.caption: In the ventral forebrain, Neurog2 restored neurons, but did not push them dorsal. The swaps were not mirror images.
scenes.visual: Ventral cells with Neurog2 make neurons that keep ventral markers. Label: not mirror images.
scenes.narration: In the ventral forebrain, Neurog2 restored neurons, but did not push them dorsal. The swaps were not mirror images.

scenes.tts: In vertebrates, the loop is a brake and a clock. The factor carries part of the identity; the tissue and the cell's history shape the rest.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: a brake, a clock, and shared identity.
scenes.narration: In vertebrates, the loop is a brake and a clock. The factor carries part of the identity; the tissue and the cell's history shape the rest.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
